subject: Fallback retainer + scaled on-call crediting — pricing and next steps
messages:
From: Greg Tanner <greg.tanner@brightbay.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbay.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: fallback retainer + scaled on-call crediting (RFP attached)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the routing/fallback demo. Procurement asked me to send over a short RFP outlining the requirement we're trying to solve and to request a pricing ballpark for two scenarios:

1) 24/7 fallback retainer to guarantee incident triage and a warm standby (8 people-equivalent) during high-impact windows.
2) A scaled on-call crediting model where we pay a monthly retainer and receive on-demand credits that deduct from the retainer as we trigger rapid-response support beyond X incidents/month.

Attached: SLA_RFP_BrightBay.pdf (PDF, 320KB) — includes sample incident profiles and expected MTTx.

High-level asks:
- Example pricing for a 6-, 12-, and 24-month term.
- How credits are consumed and replenished (monthly vs quarterly).
- Any uplift for multi-region failover (we operate in US and EU).
- Escalation path and guaranteed response windows for P1/P2.

Can you send a short proposal this week? We have a procurement review on Monday and would like a starting quote.

Best,
Greg Tanner
Head of Infrastructure
BrightBay Health
greg.tanner@brightbay.com
(415) 555-0189

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Greg Tanner <greg.tanner@brightbay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: fallback retainer + scaled on-call crediting (RFP attached)

Greg,

Thanks for the RFP — appreciated. I've sketched two practical options below that match your scenarios and included high-level economics. I'll attach a formal PDF quote (RB-quote-20260820.pdf) for procurement.

Option A — Fallback Retainer (Warm-standby)
- Monthly retainer (base): $45,000/month (covers up to 8 FTE-equivalent warm-standby; 24/7 coverage during declared incident windows).
- Incident credits: Base includes 20 rapid-response credits/month; additional credits $1,250/credit.
- Response SLA: P1 30 min initial response, P2 2 hours, P3 8 business hours.
- Multi-region failover uplift: +12% on retainer for EU coverage.
- Term discounts: 8% off for 12-month prepaid, 14% off for 24-month prepaid.

Option B — Scaled On-call Crediting (Consumption-forward)
- Monthly retainer: $18,000/month (priority routing + reserved slots).
- Credits pool: 60 credits/quarter included; credits consumed per P1/P2 event (P1=4 credits, P2=1 credit).
- Replenishment: Quarterly top-up; unused credits roll over for one quarter.
- Over-consumption: Additional credits billed at $1,400/credit; volume discount tiers at 500+ credits/yr.
- Response SLA: P1 45 min, P2 3 hours.

Additional notes:
- We recommend a 3-month pilot on Option B to baseline incident volume; we can auto-convert to Option A if BrightBay prefers guaranteed standby.
- We can commit to a contract clause for routing fallbacks (automatic failover to a cross-region pool) with documented runbook and quarterly drills.

Next steps
1) I'll attach the PDF quote and a short mutual action plan.
2) If the economics look reasonable, procurement can confirm preferred term and I'll open a DocuSign envelope.

Attached: RB-quote-20260820.pdf (quote, contains line-item pricing and T&Cs)

Would you like a brief call this afternoon to walk procurement through the crediting model?

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: fallback retainer + scaled on-call crediting — pricing and next steps

Rachel / Karthik,

Quick internal note on pricing structure before we send to Greg:
- Suggest capping per-event credits for P1 at 3 credits when retainer is 12+ months prepaid (gives them incentive to commit).
- For EU uplift, confirm currency risk mitigation — recommend invoicing in USD but offer a quarterly FX adjustment clause.
- Add an SLA exception carve-out for scheduled maintenance during major releases (48-hour notice).

Happy to hop on Greg's call. I can own the runbook appendix and ensure ops sign-off on the quarterly drills.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Greg Tanner <greg.tanner@brightbay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, BrightBay Procurement <procurement@brightbay.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: fallback retainer + scaled on-call crediting (RFP attached)

Greg,

Thanks — quick follow-up after internal alignment. A couple of clarifications and an ask before procurement review:

Clarifications
- For the pilot (Option B): we recommend a 90-day pilot with a $3,000 activation fee and a prorated first-month retainer. Credits will be tracked in the portal and you can export monthly consumption.
- Credits rollover: unused credits roll for one quarter only (no multi-quarter accumulation).
- FX: We'll invoice in USD; we can include an FX-adjustment clause but pricing will be fixed for the term.

Procurement ask
- If procurement can confirm preferred term (6/12/24) and whether BrightBay wants EU uplift included, I'll push the DocuSign with the agreed line items and MOP.

Proposed MOP (mutual action plan)
- Today (EOD): BrightBay confirms term preference and region scope.
- Mon 08/24: Procurement internal review completed.
- Tue 08/25: Joint kickoff + runbook workshop (30 min).
- Wed 08/26: DocuSign envelope executed; pilot begins within 3 business days of signature.

If that timeline works, I can set up the call for Tue AM and route the quote to DocuSign after we get confirmation.

Thanks,
Rachel
Senior Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
